# Reviewing a one-line CSS change that arrived with 140 committed PNGs

## Problem Description

I am the reviewer on PR #5311 and I have about forty minutes before the release
train. The change itself is one property in one file - our button corner radius
goes from 4px to 8px, signed off by design in FIG-882 on 2026-09-07. The PR also
carries 140 baseline PNG files that the update job produced.

Ana, who runs the web guild, has already told me in Slack to take the whole
thing as a block: "it's one token, the diffs are corners, we are not spending a
reviewer afternoon on 140 images." Dan says the same on the PR. I am inclined to
agree with both of them and click approve, and if that is the right call I want
to be told so plainly rather than handed a list of homework.

What I have instead of the images is the list of changed files with their git
status, the JSON our reporter writes (per-file pixel counts and the bounding box
of the changed region, which is why we started emitting it), the state of the
`main` tree for the same directories, the open-bug board, and the workflow that
generated the commit. That is what I want you to reason from.

Give me a per-group verdict with the evidence for each. If any of it should not
go in on this branch, tell me exactly what Dan has to run to put back only the
parts that do belong, and be specific about the command - last time someone
"just re-ran the job" here we ended up in a worse place than we started.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/visual-review-5311.md`: a verdict for every group of baseline
   files in the change, the evidence behind each verdict, ordered so the thing
   that matters most is first.
2. Give Dan the exact command or commands to run, and say what he should take
   off the branch.
3. Say what has to change so the next token-sized PR does not arrive like this.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/visual-review-5311.md`: a verdict for every group of baseline
   files in the change, the evidence behind each verdict, ordered so the thing
   that matters most is first.
2. Give Dan the exact command or commands to run, and say what he should take
   off the branch.
3. Say what has to change so the next token-sized PR does not arrive like this.
assertions: Group C is kept out of this PR, on the ground that those 18 files were written without a comparison (no prior baseline, so no diff exists for anyone to review) and therefore carry no verification of anything. Approving them, or describing them as 'fixing the red settings spec', scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Refusing them only because they are out of scope for a radius change, without stating that a first capture is written rather than compared, scores at most half.

The remediation given to Dan MUST NOT be an unscoped `npx playwright test --update-snapshots`, and MUST NOT be re-dispatching the visual-update workflow with its `spec` input left at the default empty value - either re-runs the same over-broad rewrite that produced this PR. Any command or instruction that regenerates every baseline in the suite scores zero here. Full marks require the command to be limited to the specs that legitimately change (a spec path or a grep), and to say that the regenerated files are reviewed before they land.

@atran's claim that a rename moves the PNG on disk is contradicted and the 15 Group D files are kept out. The evidence is that no PNG in the diff has status D and the 15 old-title files are byte identical on both sides, so the old baselines are still there and the new ones were captured fresh with nothing to compare against. Accepting the claim, or approving Group D as cosmetic, scores zero. Noting only that the old files are now orphaned, without saying the new ones were never compared, scores at most half.

Group B is held back for eyes-on review, with the numbers: 24106-31533 differing pixels against Group A's 88-421, in boxes 380-560px tall sitting at x 872-884, which the layout doc places in the order summary panel - a region that consumes no button radius. Accepting @dweir's 'bigger surface' explanation and approving Group B with Group A scores zero. Flagging it on pixel count alone, without the box positions or the layout evidence, scores at most half.

The review names BUG-4471 and connects it to `settings-billing-1-chromium-linux.png`: the settings spec runs against seed-acct-03, which has no payment method, so that capture records the empty card and console-error state as the expected appearance. Never surfacing this scores zero. Mentioning the bug without connecting it to a specific baseline file scores at most half.

Group A is approved as consistent with the one-token change, citing 88-421 differing pixels in 14-22px boxes no wider than 180px at button positions, with a prior baseline present for all 96. Refusing the whole PR, or sending all 140 files back, scores zero here - the deadline is real and 96 of these files are exactly what the change should produce.

The answer identifies that the workflow accepts a `spec` input and never passes it to the test command, and that `git add -A '*.png'` commits every rewritten file regardless of which spec was targeted, then fixes at least the first of those. Not mentioning the workflow at all scores zero.

docs/visual-review-5311.md exists and carries a separate, explicit verdict for each of A, B, C and D, ordered with the most serious first. A single undifferentiated verdict over all 140 files scores zero.

# Storefront visual checks flip pass/fail depending on which shard runs them

## Problem Description

Six weeks ago we widened the storefront visual coverage from "desktop only" to
four viewport widths, because the whole point of the redesign was that the
product page had to hold up at 375 through 1920. The change went in on
2026-07-29 and nobody has trusted the result since.

What we actually see:

- `tests/product-detail.spec.ts` goes red roughly one run in three, and which of
  the three checks goes red changes run to run. Re-running the job usually
  clears it, so people re-run.
- The committed PNG files keep changing **dimensions** between PRs. Somebody
  went through the history: `gallery.png` has been 375x667 in seven of the last
  fourteen PRs and 1280x800 in the other seven, and no PR in that window touched
  the gallery component.
- Chloe on design filed a bug on 2026-09-02 saying the tablet layout has had an
  overlapping price badge "for about a month". We went back and looked - every
  visual job in that month was green on the runs it passed. Nothing flagged it.

Ed added `retries: 3` in mid-August to stop the re-run requests, which reduced
the noise in the Slack channel and did nothing else.

I want the four widths independently checked, so that a tablet-only regression
is a tablet-only failure and I can tell from the job which width broke. I also
need to know what happens to the three PNG files currently committed, because I
do not believe any of them is a baseline for anything in particular. Marco's
suggestion is that we keep them and just rename each one to whichever width its
dimensions match, which would save us re-shooting three images.

Once the config is right I want to run the update job once, commit whatever
comes out, and be done with this before the sprint closes on Friday - so give me
the exact command sequence to run.

The repo, the config, a summary of what is on disk, the run history and the open
storefront bugs are attached.

## Output Specification

1. Edit `playwright.config.ts` so each of the four viewport widths is checked
   against its own baseline. Do not add or remove viewport widths.
2. Write `docs/breakpoint-baselines.md`: what was actually wrong, what has to
   happen to the three PNG files currently in `tests/__screens__/`, the exact
   command sequence to re-establish baselines, and the number of baseline files
   this suite should hold when it is correct versus the number it holds today.
3. Leave `tools/` alone. `node --test` must still pass from the repo root when
   you are finished.
evals.expected_output:
1. Edit `playwright.config.ts` so each of the four viewport widths is checked
   against its own baseline. Do not add or remove viewport widths.
2. Write `docs/breakpoint-baselines.md`: what was actually wrong, what has to
   happen to the three PNG files currently in `tests/__screens__/`, the exact
   command sequence to re-establish baselines, and the number of baseline files
   this suite should hold when it is correct versus the number it holds today.
3. Leave `tools/` alone. `node --test` must still pass from the repo root when
   you are finished.
assertions: The command sequence MUST NOT capture a tablet-768 baseline from the current page without dealing with SF-834. Handing over an unscoped `--update-snapshots` across all four projects, with no mention of the open price-badge overlap, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require either holding the tablet-768 capture until SF-834 is fixed and generating the other three projects now, or capturing it with an explicit written record that this baseline encodes a known defect plus a dated follow-up to re-capture - and in both cases naming 768 as the width inside the 720-900 band the bug reports. Advising the reviewer to 'check the diff before committing', without naming the defect or the project it lands in, scores at most half.

All three files in `tests/__screens__/` are deleted and recaptured. Marco's proposal to rename each file to the width its dimensions match is refused, on the ground that the dimensions record which project wrote last, not which project the image belongs to, and that each file has been rewritten at different sizes by PRs that touched nothing on the page. Keeping or renaming any of the three as a baseline for a specific project scores zero here. Deleting them without answering Marco scores at most half.

The new `snapshotPathTemplate` carries a per-project segment so the four viewport projects write to four different files, and retains a platform segment. A template with no project discriminator scores zero. Dropping the platform segment on the grounds that everyone is on Linux scores at most half - two MacBooks arrive in October and captures from the two platforms are not interchangeable.

The document states that all four projects resolve to the same file per check, so each run has four writers and one file per name, which is why dimensions change between PRs, why which project fails looks random, and why a re-run appears to fix it. Attributing the instability to flakiness, timing, or the runner scores zero.

The document gives both numbers explicitly: twelve baseline files when correct (four projects times three checks) against the three committed today. Giving neither, or only one of the two, scores zero.
`retries: 3` is removed, or kept with a stated reason that acknowledges it was hiding the collision rather than absorbing genuine flakiness. Leaving it in place with no comment scores zero.
`tools/run-summary.mjs` and its test file are unmodified and `node --test` still passes from the repo root. Any edit under `tools/` scores zero here.

docs/breakpoint-baselines.md exists and covers all four things asked for: the cause, the fate of the three files, the command sequence, and the counts. Missing any of the four scores at most half; producing no document scores zero.

# Every PR's visual job is red and people have started merging past it

## Problem Description

We turned on screenshot comparison for the account area three weeks ago
(2026-08-21). It has been red on every single pull request since, and as of last
Tuesday two people have admin-merged past a red visual job because they decided
it was "the screenshot thing again". That is worse than not having it.

The five of us all work on MacBooks. CI is `ubuntu-latest`. The baselines in the
repo were generated on Priya's laptop the afternoon we turned this on, and
committed in one go.

There is a thread in `docs/proposals.md` with five suggestions in it. I will say
up front that I am minded to just take P1 - it is one line, two of us have used
it at previous jobs, and I would like this off my desk before the sprint review
on Thursday. But the two people here who actually understand this stuff are on
opposite sides of it and I do not have the background to referee, so I want a
decision on each proposal by name, with the reason, and I want it implemented.

Priya is back from leave on Monday and will want to run these locally before
pushing. Tell her what she has to do differently.

The config, the spec, the workflow and a trimmed CI log are attached along with
the proposal thread.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/visual-baselines-decision.md`. Answer P1, P2, P3, P4 and P5
   individually by their identifiers, each with a verdict and the reason. State
   what a developer on a MacBook must do before pushing.
2. Implement whatever you adopt: edit `playwright.config.ts`,
   `tests/account.spec.ts` and `.github/workflows/visual.yml` as needed, and add
   any new workflow file your decision requires.
3. Say explicitly what happens to the baseline PNG files currently in the repo.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/visual-baselines-decision.md`. Answer P1, P2, P3, P4 and P5
   individually by their identifiers, each with a verdict and the reason. State
   what a developer on a MacBook must do before pushing.
2. Implement whatever you adopt: edit `playwright.config.ts`,
   `tests/account.spec.ts` and `.github/workflows/visual.yml` as needed, and add
   any new workflow file your decision requires.
3. Say explicitly what happens to the baseline PNG files currently in the repo.
assertions: P1 is refused. Adding `--update-snapshots` to the test command on the pull-request or push job MUST NOT appear anywhere in the implemented workflow. Adopting it, adopting it 'temporarily', or adopting it behind a condition that still leaves it on the gating run, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require the reason: regenerating the baseline in the same run that compares against it means the comparison is against itself, so no pixel change can ever fail - and an explicit answer to @dyoung's point that the job can still go red, namely that what survives is the non-visual assertions, not the visual coverage this job exists for. Refusing P1 with no reason, or only 'that is bad practice', scores at most half.

P5 is adopted and implemented as a separate manually-triggered workflow that regenerates on the CI platform and commits the PNGs back for review, and the answer states what makes it different from P1 - it runs outside the gating path, so the images it writes are reviewed as a diff before they become the thing future runs are compared against. Refusing P5 on the same grounds as P1 scores zero: that is a blanket objection to the flag rather than a judgement about where it runs. Adopting it without saying what distinguishes it from P1 scores at most half.

P3 is refused with the arithmetic done from the sizes in the CI log: 0.35 of the 1280 x 3160 overview is over 1.4 million pixels, and 0.35 of the 980 x 620 billing panel is over 212,000 pixels, which exceeds the panel's own content. Adopting `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.35` scores zero. Refusing it without computing what it permits on at least one of the captures scores at most half.

P2 is refused: removing the platform segment gives one file per check shared between macOS and Linux captures, which render differently in anti-aliasing, fonts and emoji, so the shared file simply loses whichever platform wrote it last and the job goes red for the other. Adopting the template as proposed scores zero. Refusing it purely on 'we might need both later', with no statement that the renderings genuinely differ, scores at most half.

The answer states plainly that the three `-chromium-darwin.png` files are deleted from the repo, and says what replaces them and where those come from. Leaving them in place, or being silent about them, scores zero. Saying 'they will be superseded' without an explicit deletion scores at most half.

The chat bubble and the sync line are hidden on the affected captures, and this is done without raising the project-wide pixel tolerance to absorb them. Solving P4 by increasing `maxDiffPixels` or `maxDiffPixelRatio` scores zero here. Agreeing with P4 in prose without changing any file scores at most half.

The upload step in `.github/workflows/visual.yml` gains `if: always()`, and the answer says why - without it the report is not uploaded on the failing run, which is the only run whose expected / actual / diff images anyone needs. Leaving the upload step unconditional-on-success scores zero here.

The document tells a developer on a MacBook what to do differently, concretely: either stop generating baselines locally and get them from the CI-side job, or run the suite in the matching container image so local captures are produced on the same platform CI uses. 'Be careful' or 'check with the team' scores zero.

docs/visual-baselines-decision.md exists and carries a separate verdict for each of P1, P2, P3, P4 and P5 under its own identifier. Answering some and skipping others, or writing one merged recommendation, scores zero.

# Taking over a visual suite that has been green for four months

## Problem Description

I inherited the web QA suite from a contractor who left in March. It has three
visual checks in `tests/visual.spec.ts` and it is basically always green, which
everybody here treats as good news.

The thing I actually want fixed is the chat bubble. It sits bottom-right on
every page, it moves, and it is in every committed baseline image. The
contractor set up hiding for it in `playwright.config.ts` back in June - it is
right there in the file - and it plainly has not taken. Priya's read is that the
images were captured before that config landed and have never been re-shot, so
she wants me to run the update job and be done with it. That is a five-minute
job and I would like to do it, but she also thought last quarter's flake was a
caching problem, so please tell me if she is wrong.

On top of that there are five requests sitting in `docs/hide-requests.md` from
three different people, all of the form "this thing moves, hide it". I do not
know which of those are reasonable and which are people trying to make a red
check go away, and I would rather not find out the hard way. I want a verdict on
each one with the reason, including the ones you turn down.

There is a report-parsing helper in `tools/` with its own tests. It has nothing
to do with any of this; leave it alone and leave it passing.

## Output Specification

1. Edit `playwright.config.ts` and `tests/visual.spec.ts` so that the hiding the
   team has asked for actually applies to every check, adding any new file that
   requires. Keep three checks covering the same three pages; do not delete
   coverage.
2. Write `docs/hide-decisions.md`: a verdict on R1 through R5 by identifier,
   each with the reason it was granted or turned down.
3. Say what has to happen to the committed baseline PNG files, and in what
   order relative to the rest of your change.
4. `node --test` must still pass from the repo root and `tools/` must not be
   edited.
